newsitem.title: HUNGARY: OTP 's share of Hungary loans falls in '96.
newsitem.headline: OTP 's share of Hungary loans falls in '96.

text.p: The overall market share in lending of OTP, Hungary's largest commercial bank decreased in 1996, OTP said on Tuesday.
Gyorgy Fenyo, OTP Director for Investor Relations told Reuters OTP's market share was some 24 percent in 1996 against about 21 percent in 1995.
Fenyo said that the bank's market share in retail loans dropped to 68 percent in 1996 from 69 percent in 1995.
OTP's market share in corporate lending was unchanged at 11 percent in 1996, while in municipal loans it fell to 71 percent from 77 percent in 1995, he added.
OTP earlier said in a statement that it boosted the volume of its lending to corporations in 1996, while its retail and municipal loans decreased.
Loans extended to corporations grew by 35.8 percent in 1996, OTP said, adding that the share of loans to small businesses dropped to 9.9 percent from 13.6 percent.
Retail loans dropped by 8.3 percent, the bank said.

"(This fall) was due to the high repayment rate of housing loans granted under conditions valid before 1994 since the amount of repayments exceeds loans granted based on the new terms," the bank said.
Municipal loans decreased by 29.1 percent in 1996, OTP said.

"The decline in municipal loans was a universal phenomenon and the result of legislative changes combined with (the municipalities') increased income from privatisation widely used for loan repayments," the bank said.
OTP's assets totalled 1,259.2 billion forints on December 31, 1996, 17.4 percent higher than in 1995, the bank said.
Fenyo said OTP's share in the total assets of Hungarian banks dropped to 28.1 percent in 1996 from 29.2 percent in 1995.
The bank posted a pre-tax profit of 12.68 billion forints in 1996, 44.8 percent more than in 1995, OTP said in the statement.
All the figures and percentages were non-consolidated, unaudited and were calculated according to the Hungarian accounting standard.
Hungary's inflation averaged 23.6 percent last year.
